questions.question_text:
Figure 1 shows a metal cube which is expanding uniformly as it is heated.
At time $t$ seconds, the length of each edge of the cube is $x$ cm, and the volume of the cube is $V\,\mathrm{cm}^3$.
(a) Show that $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=3x^2$
(1)
Given that the volume, $V\,\mathrm{cm}^3$, increases at a constant rate of $0.048\,\mathrm{cm}^3\mathrm{s}^{-1}$,
(b) find $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$, when $x=8$
(2)
(c) find the rate of increase of the total surface area of the cube, in $\mathrm{cm}^2\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, when $x=8$
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $V=x^3 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dV}{dx}=3x^2$ * cso B1 (1)
(b) $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{dx}{dV}\times\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{0.048}{3x^2}$ M1
At $x=8$: $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac{0.048}{3(8^2)}=0.00025\ (\mathrm{cm\,s}^{-1})$ ($2.5\times10^{-4}$) A1 (2)
(c) $S=6x^2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dS}{dx}=12x$ B1
$\dfrac{dS}{dt}=\dfrac{dS}{dx}\times\dfrac{dx}{dt}=12x\left(\dfrac{0.048}{3x^2}\right)$ M1
At $x=8$: $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=0.024\ (\mathrm{cm}^2\mathrm{s}^{-1})$ A1 (3)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the binomial expansion of $\mathrm{f}(x)$ in ascending powers of $x$, up to and including the term in $x^3$. Give each coefficient in its simplest form.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\mathrm{f}(x)=\dots(\dots-\dots x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ M1
$=6\times 9^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\dots)$ $\frac{6}{9^{\frac12}}, \frac{6}{3}, 2$ or equivalent B1
$=\dots\left(1+\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)(kx);+\frac{\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac32\right)}{2}(kx)^2+\frac{\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac32\right)\left(-\frac52\right)}{3!}(kx)^3+\dots\right)$ M1; A1ft
$=2\left(1+\frac{2}{9}x+\dots\right)$ or $2+\frac49 x$ A1
$=2+\frac{4}{9}x+\frac{4}{27}x^2+\frac{40}{729}x^3+\dots$ A1 (6)

$=6\times 9^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\dots)$ $\frac{6}{9^{\frac12}}, \frac{6}{3}, 2$ or equivalent B1
$=\dots\left(1+\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)(kx);+\frac{\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac32\right)}{2}(kx)^2+\frac{\left(-\frac12\right)\left(-\frac32\right)\left(-\frac52\right)}{3!}(kx)^3+\dots\right)$ M1; A1ft
$=2\left(1+\frac{2}{9}x+\dots\right)$ or $2+\frac49 x$ A1

(b) $\mathrm{g}(x)=2-\frac49 x+\frac{4}{27}x^2-\frac{40}{729}x^3+\dots$ B1ft (1)

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Differentiating implicitly to obtain $\pm ay^2\frac{dy}{dx}$ and/or $\pm bx^2\frac{dy}{dx}$ M1
$48y^2\frac{dy}{dx}+\dots-54\dots$ A1
$9x^2y\to 9x^2\frac{dy}{dx}+18xy$ or equivalent B1
$\left(48y^2+9x^2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}+18xy-54=0$ M1
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{54-18xy}{48y^2+9x^2}\ \left(=\dfrac{18-6xy}{16y^2+3x^2}\right)$ A1 (5)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the coordinates of the points on $C$ where $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $18-6xy=0$ M1
Using $x=\dfrac{3}{y}$ or $y=\dfrac{3}{x}$
$16y^3+9\left(\dfrac{3}{y}\right)^2y-54\left(\dfrac{3}{y}\right)=0$ or $16\left(\dfrac{3}{x}\right)^3+9x^2\left(\dfrac{3}{x}\right)-54x=0$ M1
Leading to $16y^4+81-162=0$ or $16+x^4-2x^4=0$ M1
$y^4=\dfrac{81}{16}$ or $x^4=16$
$y=\dfrac{3}{2},-\dfrac{3}{2}$ or $x=2,-2$ A1 A1
Substituting either of their values into $xy=3$ to obtain a value of the other variable. M1
$\left(2,\dfrac{3}{2}\right), \left(-2,-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ both A1 (7)

questions.stem:
Figure 2 shows a sketch of the curve $C$ with parametric equations
$x=(\sqrt{3})\sin 2t, \quad y=4\cos^2 t, \quad 0 \leqslant t \leqslant \pi$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=k(\sqrt{3})\tan 2t$, where $k$ is a constant to be determined.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2\sqrt{3}\cos 2t$ B1
$\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-8\cos t\sin t$ M1 A1
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-8\cos t\sin t}{2\sqrt{3}\cos 2t}$ M1
$=-\dfrac{4\sin 2t}{2\sqrt{3}\cos 2t}$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{3}\tan 2t\ \left(k=-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)$ A1 (5)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find an equation of the tangent to $C$ at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Give your answer in the form $y=ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) When $t=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$: $x=\dfrac{3}{2}, y=1$ can be implied B1
$m=-\dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{3}\tan\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\ (=2)$ M1
$y-1=2\left(x-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ M1
$y=2x-2$ A1 (4)

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $x=\sqrt{3}\sin 2t=\sqrt{3}\times 2\sin t\cos t$ M1
$x^2=12\sin^2 t\cos^2 t=12(1-\cos^2 t)\cos^2 t$
$x^2=12\left(1-\dfrac{y}{4}\right)\dfrac{y}{4}$ or equivalent M1 A1 (3)

Alternative to (c):
$y=2\cos 2t+2$ M1
$\sin^2 2t+\cos^2 2t=1$
$\dfrac{x^2}{3}+\dfrac{(y-2)^2}{4}=1$ M1 A1 (3)

questions.stem:
Figure 3 shows a sketch of part of the curve with equation $y=x^{\frac12}\ln 2x$.
The finite region $R$, shown shaded in Figure 3, is bounded by the curve, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=1$ and $x=4$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Use the trapezium rule, with 3 strips of equal width, to find an estimate for the area of $R$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4\\ \hline y & \ln 2 & \sqrt{2}\ln 4 & \sqrt{3}\ln 6 & 2\ln 8\\ \hline & 0.6931 & 1.9605 & 3.1034 & 4.1589\\ \hline\end{array}$ M1
Area $=\frac12\times 1(\dots)$ B1
$\approx \dots (0.6931+2(1.9605+3.1034)+4.1589)$ M1
$\approx \frac12\times 14.97989\dots \approx 7.49$ 7.49 cao A1 (4)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\int x^{\frac12}\ln 2x\,dx=\frac23 x^{\frac32}\ln 2x-\int \frac23 x^{\frac32}\times \frac1x\,dx$ M1 A1
$=\frac23 x^{\frac32}\ln 2x-\int \frac23 x^{\frac12}\,dx$
$=\frac23 x^{\frac32}\ln 2x-\frac49 x^{\frac32}\ (+C)$ M1 A1 (4)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Hence find the exact area of $R$, giving your answer in the form $a\ln 2+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are exact constants.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\left[\frac23 x^{\frac32}\ln 2x-\frac49 x^{\frac32}\right]_{1}^{4}=\left(\frac23 4^{\frac32}\ln 8-\frac49 4^{\frac32}\right)-\left(\frac23\ln 2-\frac49\right)$ M1
$=(16\ln 2-\dots)-\dots$ Using or implying $\ln 2^n=n\ln 2$ M1
$=\frac{46}{3}\ln 2-\frac{28}{9}$ A1 (3)
